questions.prompt: What is the first step in solving $ 2\sqrt{x+1} = 4 $?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: First isolate the radical by dividing by 2, giving $ \sqrt{x+1} = 2 $.
hints: You need to get the radical alone.
Look at the coefficient of the square root.

questions.prompt: After solving a radical equation, you must check for ___ solutions that may have been introduced by squaring.
hints: They don't satisfy the original equation.
Square both sides and solve, then check each.
One of the apparent solutions will make one side negative.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an extraneous solution to $ x = \sqrt{x+6} $?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: $ x = -2 $ gives $ -2 = \sqrt{4} $, which is false. So $ -2 $ is extraneous.
The equation simplifies to $ 2x+5 = x+7 $, giving $ x = 2 $.

questions.prompt: To isolate $ x $ in $ x^{3/2} = 8 $, you raise both sides to which power?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Raising to $ 2/3 $ cancels the $ 3/2 $, giving $ x = 8^{2/3} = 4 $.

questions.prompt: For the square root inequality $ \sqrt{x-3} < 2 $, the radicand must be at least ___.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The solution is $ 1 \le x \le 5 $, so the maximum is 5.
